title: Full Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm with termination proof

problemStatement.formal: \text{Define the Moser-Tardos resampling algorithm } \mathcal{A} \text{ on bad events } A_1, \dots, A_m \text{ over independent variables } V_1, \dots, V_n. \text{ Prove: if } \exists x_i \in [0,1) \text{ with } \Pr[A_i] \le x_i \prod_{k \sim i} (1-x_k), \text{ then } \mathbb{E}[\#\text{resamplings of } A_i] \le x_i/(1-x_i).
problemStatement.plain: Currently `Proofs/LovaszLocalLemma.lean` only states the non-negativity of the Moser–Tardos bound Σ x_i/(1-x_i) (theorem `moser_tardos_termination`). The actual Moser–Tardos theorem says this is an *upper bound on the expected number of resamplings* of the constructive algorithm. OQ-01 defines the algorithm, the probability space, and proves the bound.
whyMatters: Crown jewel of the constructive probabilistic method: turns the LLL from a pure-existence theorem into a polynomial-time randomised algorithm
Bridges the symmetric/general LLL (already formalised) with explicit algorithm design (k-SAT, Latin squares, hypergraph colouring)
First-ever machine-checked construction of an LLL avoidance procedure would be a marquee result

proven: Moser & Tardos (2010) — J. ACM 57(2) — the canonical published proof via the witness-tree construction
Moser (2009, STOC) — original entropy-compression argument for the symmetric case
Symmetric / general LLL itself (parent `prob-method-lovasz-local`) — 364 lines, 0 sorries
open: No Lean formalisation of the Moser–Tardos algorithm or its termination proof exists in Mathlib4 or any visible gallery (as of 2026-05-12)
Galton–Watson branching processes are not in Mathlib (workaround: direct generating-function calculation)
knownResults.goal: Define the algorithm as a PMF-based Markov chain on configurations and prove the witness-tree-based bound E[#resamplings of A_i] ≤ x_i/(1-x_i).

S2: encoding typeclass requirements (`Fintype` / `Nonempty` / `Decidable`) as MTProblem structure fields with `attribute [instance]` lets the namespace's API (`P.State`, `P.isViolated`, `P.pickBad`) compile as a single uniform surface; pickBad uses `Finset.min'` on the filter of `isBad`-violated indices as the canonical deterministic resampling rule

S2: `LLLAdmissible` packages the LLL inequality at the algebraic-rational level (auxiliary `prob, adj`) so that the faithful link to the actual uniform-draw measure can be a separate OQ-01-A.2 lemma — decouples the algorithm-shell from the measure-theoretic faithful link

For `P.State = (j : Fin n) → P.alphabet j` with `alphabet j : Type` having only `[Fintype] + [Nonempty]` field-instances, the Pi measurable-space chain does not fire — prerequisite gap one layer deeper than typical `gh api` bearer audits catch.

S8: `PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_fintype` (Basic.lean:203) is the cheaper substitute for faithful-link lemmas — requires only `[Fintype α]`, no `[MeasurableSpace]`, no `MeasurableSet s`. Outer-measure form is the load-bearing faithful link; `toMeasure` corollary is +8 LOC via `local instance` plumbing only when downstream actually needs `toMeasure` (e.g., OQ-01-B witness-tree integration with measure-theoretic API).
